subject: Human Evolution
title: Calibrating with Fossils
description: Learn Calibrating with Fossils in one minute.

hook.text: Molecular clocks need anchors. Without known fossil dates, mutation rates are just guesses floating in time.

buildup.text: Scientists calibrate clocks using well-dated fossils—like the human-orangutan split anchored at 12–16 million years.

discovery.text: Different calibration points can shift all downstream date estimates, sometimes dramatically.

twist.text: New fossil discoveries regularly force recalibration—the clock is always being tuned, never perfectly set.

climax.text: Molecular clocks and fossils correct each other in a feedback loop—each alone is incomplete.

punchline.text: Bones set the clock. DNA reads the time.

quiz.question: How are molecular clocks calibrated?
options: Using well-dated fossil divergence points as anchors
